words.meaning: Old word from andrapodizw (from anhr, man, pouv, foot, to catch by the foot), to enslave. So enslavers, whether kidnappers (men-stealers) of free men or stealers of the slaves of other men. So slave-dealers. By the use of this word Paul deals a blow at the slave-trade (cf. Philemon). (Robertson's NT Word Pictures)
words.plain: Men-stealers [the Greek word] literally means 'to catch a person by the foot' — dragging them away against their will. It refers to enslavers: kidnappers of free people, or those who stole slaves belonging to someone else — slave-dealers of every kind. By using this word, Paul strikes directly at the slave trade.
